title: Chaos-resilient routing policy for staged model rollouts
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: During staged model rollouts (canary / A-B) we observe unsafe user reassignment and poor rollback behaviour when partial regional failures, capacity heterogeneity, or ephemeral control-plane latencies occur. Existing pinning logic is deterministic but brittle: it can over-pin to capacity-constrained variants, lose session stickiness on control-plane timeouts, and produce noisy user experiences when fallback variants have subtle tokenizer/semantic incompatibilities.

Goal: Introduce a chaos-resilient routing policy layer that acts as a set of guardrails around model-version pinning and rollout splits. The layer should ensure that: (1) canary exposures are strictly quota limited and reversible with minimal user impact, (2) fallback variant selection prioritizes compatibility and graceful degradation, (3) region and tier routing cooperate with pinning to avoid hot spots, and (4) rollout safety withstands transient infra failures (region partial outage, scheduler lag, DB inconsistency).

Scope: This ticket covers design and implementation of the routing "safety checks" stage, a compatibility-scored fallback matrix, session pin TTL strategy, circuit-breaker thresholds, and rollout enrollment quotas. It also covers API flags for "rollback-safe shadow" mode and observability instrumentation (metrics and tracing) to validate safety properties.

Non-goals: Rewriting the serving runtime or changing model weights/quantization. This work focuses on routing policies and orchestration only.
acceptance_criteria: New routing safety stage exists in the request pipeline and is exercised by canary flows
Canary enrollment honors a configurable quota and does not exceed the allocated capacity percentage for a tier/region
Session pin TTL semantics implemented: short TTL for early canaries, graduated TTL increase on stable cohorts
Fallback selection uses a compatibility score (tokenizer compatibility, model architecture family, last-stable-rollback distance) and chooses safe variants under failures
Circuit-breaker triggers cause automatic fallback to pre-defined safe variant and emit an alert with runbook link
Observability: per-route canary-exposure, fallback-reasons histogram, rollback incidence, and recovery time dashboards available
E2E chaos tests (simulated region partial outage and control-plane lag) pass in staging with no >1% increase in 5xx errors for non-canary traffic
implementation_plan: Design RFC: propose API for safety checks and fallback-scoring (owner: Marco) — complete by 2026-03-03
Routing resolver change: add 'pre-pin safety' stage that evaluates capacity and compatibility and returns a routing action rather than a raw pin
Quota system: use existing rate-limiter to gate canary enrollments; extend with per-cohort counters and time-windowed quotas
Session TTLs: implement graduated TTL logic in session-store layer with deterministic seed-based cohort assignment
Fallback matrix: compute compatibility score at model onboarding and persist in catalog; scoring heuristic includes tokenizer delta, head-count match, and empirical eval regression margin
Circuit-breaker: implement thresholded breaker tied to region-tier token error-rate and request-latency percentiles
Observability: add metrics (canary_enrolled, canary_quota_exhausted, fallback_used, fallback_reason, cb_open_duration) and tracing annotations
Docs & Runbooks: write operational playbook for rollback and for triaging fallback reasons
updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting — agreed safety stage should be idempotent and re-entrant. Decided deterministic seeding for cohort assignment to make tests reproducible. (Aisha)
2026-03-01: RFC draft posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Routing/chaos-resilient-routing-rfc — feedback requested from runtime and product teams. (Marco)
2026-03-04: Runtime review: suggested moving compatibility scoring computation to offline onboarding to avoid per-request CPU cost. Action: design a lightweight cached score payload. (Runtime team)
2026-03-07: Prototype implemented for safety stage in local dev; uses existing rate-limiter and a stubbed fallback matrix. Basic unit tests added. (Marco)

2026-03-10: Integration test failure discovered: session TTL extension logic caused unexpected pin migration during small-scale canary; root cause: TTL refresh path conflated session-heartbeat with pin-grant. Added fix and additional assertion. (Marco)

2026-03-12: Staging load tests scheduled (chaos scenario): simulated region latency spike + 20% capacity evaporation. Test expected 95% of canary traffic to continue but be limited to quota; non-canary 5xx should remain <1%.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Compatibility scores may misclassify and route to a variant that causes visible regressions. Mitigation: require a minimum empirical eval margin and a human approval gate for any cross-family fallback entries.

Risk: Per-request safety checks add latency. Mitigation: compute heavy parts at onboarding and cache score payloads; keep pre-pin check under a few hundred microseconds by using heuristic short-circuits.

Risk: Quota exhaustion during traffic spikes may starve canary cohort and hurt signal collection. Mitigation: quota windows aligned with autoscaler metrics and allow temporary burst tokens if capacity is detected available for >60s.
Risk: Circuit-breaker flaps in noisy conditions. Mitigation: Hysteresis and multi-metric guard (error-rate + latency) before open; automated short window rollbacks to safe variant not full outage.
Risk: Operational complexity for SREs and support. Mitigation: clear dashboards, per-route rollbacks, and a one-click internal console control to disable safety stage for emergencies.
testing_plan: Unit tests for safety stage decision tree and session TTL transitions
Integration test: staged-canary pipeline with stubbed fallback matrix and quota enforcement
Staging chaos test: simulate region partial outage (30% capacity loss) and control-plane DB lag (500ms) while running canary at 2% enrollment
Backfill regression suite: run existing smoke prompts against canary and fallback variants; flag semantic drift >3% on evaluation metrics
Load test: ensure safety-stage adds <5ms p95 latency at 1000 RPS in staging
Runbook drills: SRE on-call performs rollback and recovery exercises using the one-click console control
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary internal): enable safety stage in staging only and run canary flows at 0.5% internal traffic for 72h
Phase 1 (beta customers): opt-in for 1% external traffic with rollout quotas and extra logging for two customers; monitor metrics for 7 days
Phase 2 (gradual ramp): 1% -> 5% -> 10% over 2 weeks if stability metrics hold; automated rollback triggers defined for each step
Phase 3 (default): safety stage enabled for all rollouts, default TTLs set to graduated mode; deprecation window for legacy pinning behavior is 60 days
Rollback behavior: immediate fallback to last-stable variant on CB open or if fallback_score<threshold; automatic cohort drain with session TTL shortened to forced-evict window
